VIETSTYLE COMMERCE
INVENTORY MANAGEMENT POLICY MANUAL
Document ID: INV-MAN-001Version: v1.0 | 16/10/2026Scope: fashion, streetwear, and outdoor SKUs; retail / e-commerce

Columns: SIMULATION DOCUMENT FOR DATATHON 2026. Operating thresholds, lead times, KPIs, and approval levels are simulated proposals that must be approved by the business owner before real-world use. The dataset does not clearly specify currency and does not provide inbound PO, warehouse-level inventory, or backorder data. Do not treat sample results as current inventory figures.

1. Purpose and Principles
This document defines inventory controls from replenishment planning through receiving, storage, cycle counting, returns processing, and disposal. The objective is to balance product availability, holding costs, tied-up capital, and data accuracy.
Maintain one source of truth for each SKU; every adjustment must have an audit trail.
Do not automatically issue a purchase order (PO) when on-hand quantity, stockout signals, and days of supply conflict.
Separate the duties of the counter, the person entering adjustments, and the approver.
Distinguish observed dataset values from policy parameters assumed for simulation.
AI only supports queries and recommendations; purchasing, write-off, and disposal decisions require an accountable human.

2. Scope and Data Basis
The dataset contains 2,412 SKUs in products.csv and 60,247 records in inventory.csv, covering 2012-07-31 through 2022-12-31. The latest snapshot is 2022-12-31, with records for 424 SKUs. Observed categories include Streetwear, Outdoor, Casual, and GenZ. Sales.csv covers 2012-07-04 through 2022-12-31. Returns, orders, promotions, and delivery data may support root-cause analysis but do not replace the inventory ledger.
The dataset does not fully provide inbound purchase orders, MOQ, supplier lead times, backorders, warehouse locations, or a confirmed currency. These fields must be added before implementing purchasing policies in a real environment.

Section: 3. Roles and Responsibilities
Columns: Role | Primary Responsibility
Row 1: Role: Inventory Manager | Primary Responsibility: Owns KPIs, inventory thresholds, exceptions, and policy approvals.
Row 2: Role: Inventory Controller / Planner | Primary Responsibility: Calculates demand, reorder point (ROP), and target stock; reviews alerts and prepares PO proposals.
Row 3: Role: Procurement | Primary Responsibility: Manages suppliers, minimum order quantities (MOQ), lead times, POs, and delivery schedule confirmations.
Row 4: Role: Warehouse Supervisor | Primary Responsibility: Handles receiving, put-away, cycle counts, variance investigations, and operational discipline.
Row 5: Role: Returns QA | Primary Responsibility: Inspects returned goods and classifies them for resale, repair, quarantine, or disposal.
Row 6: Role: Finance | Primary Responsibility: Reconciles cost of goods, adjusts inventory value, and approves write-offs within delegated authority.

Section: 3. Roles and Responsibilities
Columns: Role | Primary Responsibility
Row 7: Role: System / Data Owner | Primary Responsibility: Manages access permissions, data-field definitions, logs, and AI controls.

4. Replenishment Policy
Reference model for SKUs with relatively stable demand:
Inventory position = On-hand + Open PO − Backorder
Reorder Point (ROP) = Daily demand × (Lead time + Safety days)
Target Stock = Daily demand × (Lead time + Safety days + Review period)
Initial simulation assumptions: 14-day lead time, 7 days of safety stock, and a 7-day review period. These values may be adjusted by supplier or product category; the lead time is not derived from the data.
Review replenishment proposals at least weekly and before promotional campaigns.
Before issuing a PO, check available inventory, open POs, held stock, backorders, MOQ, budget, and delivery schedule.
If a stockout signal occurs alongside more than 120 days of supply, do not automatically reorder; open a P1 investigation.
Do not replenish SKUs with more than 120 days of supply unless there is an approved campaign, customer commitment, or documented justification.
Every emergency PO must document the reason, service impact, and approver.

Section: 5. ABC Classification and Cycle Count Schedule
Columns: Class | Reference Criteria | Frequency | Investigation SLA
Row 1: Class: A | Reference Criteria: SKUs contributing approximately 80% of annual consumption value | Frequency: Weekly | Investigation SLA: Investigate variances the same day
Row 2: Class: B | Reference Criteria: Next group contributing approximately 15% | Frequency: Monthly | Investigation SLA: Investigate within 2 business days
Row 3: Class: C | Reference Criteria: Remaining approximately 5% | Frequency: Quarterly | Investigation SLA: Investigate within 5 business days

Section: 5. ABC Classification and Cycle Count Schedule
ABC classification must be based on annual consumption value (annual demand × cost), not sales volume alone. When demand history is insufficiently reliable, use provisional classes and review after three cycles.

Section: 6. Operating Thresholds and KPIs
Columns: KPI | Simulated Target / Threshold | Action
Row 1: KPI: Fill rate | Simulated Target / Threshold: Simulated target ≥ 98% | Action: Below 95%: P1 alert and root-cause analysis
Row 2: KPI: Days of supply | Simulated Target / Threshold: Reference: 28–60 days depending on category | Action: >120 days: overstock review; >180 days: mandatory handling plan
Row 3: KPI: Inventory record accuracy | Simulated Target / Threshold: Simulated target ≥ 98% | Action: High-value or recurring variances: investigate root cause
Row 4: KPI: Stockout rate | Simulated Target / Threshold: Simulated target <2% of SKU lines per day | Action: Track actual stockouts separately from data flags
Row 5: KPI: Aged / slow-moving stock | Simulated Target / Threshold: No inventory over 180 days without a plan | Action: Transfer, bundle, markdown, or dispose with approval

Section: 6. Operating Thresholds and KPIs
These KPI targets are initial simulation values and must be calibrated to the business's service levels, margins, and inventory strategy.

7. Excess and Slow-Moving Inventory
Over 120 days of supply: pause replenishment and review the forecast, inventory by size/color, in-transit goods, and campaign plans.
Over 180 days: Merchandising prepares a plan for transfers, bundling, controlled markdowns, or disposal.
Over 240 days: the Inventory Manager and Finance assess inventory write-downs or disposal under accounting rules.
Do not default to discounting when the root cause is bad data, incorrect size allocation, or held orders.

8. Receiving, Returns, and Quarantine
Match the PO, SKU, size, color, quantity, packaging condition, and delivery documents.
Record shortages, overages, or damage before confirming receipt; photos and an incident report are required for exceptions.
Returned goods must remain in QUARANTINE until inspected by QA; do not add them to available-to-promise inventory before they meet the release criteria.
A-grade: return to sale; B-grade: repair or repackage if approved; C-grade: segregate for supplier return, scrapping, or write-off.
Assign return-reason codes (e.g., wrong size, product defect, late delivery) to inform Merchandising, QA, and Logistics.

9. Promotions and Seasonality
At least four weeks before a campaign, Merchandising and the Planner agree on forecasts by SKU, size, and color.
Check promotions.csv or the campaign system for start/end dates, channel, discount, minimum-order conditions, and stackable_flag.
Increase target stock only when supported by a forecast or approval; do not order based solely on traffic or total revenue.
After the campaign, compare the forecast with sell-through, remaining stock, and return rate to update the plan.

Section: 10. Approvals and Exception Handling
Columns: Decision Type | Approval Flow | Timing
Row 1: Decision Type: PO proposal within budget and approved parameters | Approval Flow: Planner → Procurement Manager | Timing: Per current purchasing procedure
Row 2: Decision Type: PO exceeding budget, new SKU, or unusual campaign | Approval Flow: Procurement Manager → Operations + Finance | Timing: Before PO issuance
Row 3: Decision Type: Small inventory adjustment with sufficient evidence | Approval Flow: Counter ≠ data-entry person → Warehouse Supervisor | Timing: Within 1 business day
Row 4: Decision Type: Large or recurring adjustment, or suspected fraud | Approval Flow: Inventory Controller + Finance / Operations | Timing: Hold related transactions and investigate
Row 5: Decision Type: Disposal / scrap / write-down | Approval Flow: QA + Inventory Manager + Finance | Timing: According to financial authority

11. Data Quality Controls
In inventory.csv, 67.3% of records have stockout_flag=1, 76.3% have overstock_flag=1, 30,495 records have both flags enabled, and the total reorder_flag is zero. In the 2022-12-31 snapshot, 232 SKUs have both stockout_flag and overstock_flag enabled. These are signals requiring verification, not proof that each SKU is simultaneously understocked and overstocked.
Recalculate days of supply from available stock and average demand; retain both the original and recalculated values.
Verify the definitions of stockout_flag, overstock_flag, and reorder_flag before using them for decisions.
Record the source file, snapshot date, formula, update timestamp, and data owner.
When signals conflict, set the status to DATA CONFLICT, block automatic POs, and require verification by the Inventory Controller.
Do not allow AI to modify source data or issue POs autonomously. AI answers must state the snapshot date, source, and confidence level.

12. Required Records and Retention
Purchase requests / POs and approvals.
Receiving reports, exception photos, and supplier documents.
Count sheets, variances, causes, and adjustment approvals.
Return records, QA results, and disposition.
KPI reports, exception logs, parameter changes, and audit trails.

Appendix A — Machine-Readable Policy Table
Policy IDs INV-POL-001 through INV-POL-012 are exported separately in policy_rules.csv for lookup, knowledge-base ingestion, or Enterprise Knowledge AI Agent testing. For RAG, each chunk should keep policy_id, owner, trigger, action, SLA, and approval together.

Appendix B — Simulation Limitations
The latest snapshot in the dataset is 2022-12-31; it is not current inventory.
The 14-day lead time, 7-day safety stock, and 7-day review period are assumed, adjustable parameters.
Average demand in the workbook uses up to the three most recent available snapshots for each SKU; the snapshots are not necessarily consecutive months.
Inbound PO and backorder data are unavailable; the workbook defaults both fields to zero and requires users to enter values before making decisions.
The dataset does not specify the currency for price/COGS; do not use these values as monetary approval limits until the currency is confirmed.

Row 2: Policy ID: INV-POL-002 | Policy: Replenishment | Trigger: Inventory position <= reorder point, with no unresolved data alerts | Action bắt buộc: Propose a PO based on target stock; check open POs, backorders, MOQ, and budget before submitting for approval | Owner: Planner + Procurement | SLA / Frequency: Review weekly | Approval: Per purchasing authority limits

Row 4: Policy ID: INV-POL-004 | Policy: ABC Cycle Counting | Trigger: A/B/C SKUs classified by annual consumption value | Action bắt buộc: A: weekly; B: monthly; C: quarterly; use blind counts and independent reconciliation | Owner: Warehouse Supervisor | SLA / Frequency: As scheduled | Approval: Variances above threshold require approval

Row 5: Policy ID: INV-POL-005 | Policy: Inventory Adjustment | Trigger: A variance exists between physical count and system quantity | Action bắt buộc: Do not adjust without a report, reason code, and evidence; separate the counter and approver | Owner: Warehouse Supervisor + Inventory Controller | SLA / Frequency: Within 1 business day | Approval: Large variances require Finance/Operations
Row 6: Policy ID: INV-POL-006 | Policy: Excess / Slow-Moving Inventory | Trigger: Calculated days of supply >120 days; a handling plan is required above 180 days | Action bắt buộc: Stop replenishment; review transfers, bundles, markdowns, or disposal while protecting margin | Owner: Merchandising + Procurement | SLA / Frequency: Review monthly | Approval: Markdowns subject to pricing authority

VIETSTYLE COMMERCE INVENTORY CONTROL POLICY & OPERATING MODEL Policy • Procedures • Inventory • Exceptions • Data Controls v1.0 | 16 Oct 2026 | Datathon 2026 Simulation For training and process design; this is not an approved policy. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 1

01 | Data Context The dataset is for simulation and does not reflect current inventory. 2,412 SKUs in product master 60,247 Inventory records across snapshots 424 SKUs in the 2022-12-31 snapshot 67.3% Records with stockout_flag enabled Product categories • Streetwear • Outdoor • Casual • GenZ Data quality issues requiring control • 76.3% bản ghi bật overstock_flag • 30,495 bản ghi bật đồng thời stockout + overstock • reorder_flag có tổng bằng 0 • Snapshot mới nhất trong file: 2022-12-31 VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 2

02 | Operating Model Separate decision-making authority from data-entry operations. PLAN Forecast / campaign ROP & target stock → APPROVE Budget / supplier PO authorization → RECEIVE PO match QC & put-away → CONTROL Cycle count Exception handling → LEARN KPI / root cause Forecast update Control principle: the counter ≠ the adjustment-entry person ≠ the approver. The AI Agent may only read authorized data and make recommendations; it must not issue POs or modify inventory autonomously. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 3

03 | Replenishment Rules Default parameters are for simulation only and must be replaced with supplier data. Formulas Inventory Position = On-hand + Open PO − Backorder ROP = Daily Demand × (Lead Time + Safety Days) Target = Daily Demand × (Lead Time + Safety Days + Review Period) INITIAL PARAMETERS Lead time: 14 days Safety stock: 7 days Review period: 7 days Reorder trigger: Inventory Position ≤ ROP If a stockout/service signal exists while calculated days of supply >120 days → DATA CONFLICT. Block automatic PO recommendations and verify transactions and demand before purchasing. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 4

04 | Cycle Counting & Adjustments ABC is based on annual consumption value, not quantity alone. GROUP A ~80% of consumption value Weekly GROUP B Next ~15% Monthly GROUP C Remaining ~5% Quarterly Process: prepare list → blind count → independent recount → reconcile receipts/picks/returns/transfers → record cause → approve → adjust with an audit trail. Never delete old transactions; every adjustment needs a ticket ID, data-entry person, approver, timestamp, and evidence. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 5

05 | Excess Stock, Returns & Quarantine High inventory does not mean goods are available for sale. DAYS OF SUPPLY >120 Pause replenishment; check the forecast, size/color mix, and in-transit goods. >180 DAYS Plan transfers, bundles, markdowns, or approved disposal. RETURNS Quarantine → QA → A-grade resale / B-grade repair / C-grade handled separately. Returned goods may be added to available inventory only after QA confirms condition and updates disposition. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 6

06 | Promotions & KPIs Inventory must be planned before a campaign launches. Before campaign (T−4 weeks) • Forecast by SKU / size / color • Check stock, POs, lead time, and MOQ • Confirm discount, channel, and stackable flag • Approve target-stock increases if needed After campaign • Sell-through / remaining stock • Return rate and return reasons • Forecast error and corrective actions Fill rate ≥98% simulated target Inventory accuracy ≥98% simulated target Stockout rate <2% simulated target Aged stock >180 days requires a plan KPIs are simulated thresholds and must be calibrated to margin and service levels. VietStyle Commerce • Datathon 2026 • Simulation Document 7

07 | Clean Data Before Automation For the Inventory / RAG Agent 1. Giữ snapshot date và source file. 2. Trả lời kèm policy_id và trích dẫn nguồn. 3. Không suy đoán lead time / currency / PO. 4. Mâu thuẫn → DATA CONFLICT. 5. Không tự ghi PO hoặc điều chỉnh tồn. Implementation Roadmap • Chuẩn hóa master SKU / size / color • Xác nhận định nghĩa flags và đơn vị đo • Bổ sung PO inbound, backorder, lead time, MOQ • Pilot trên nhóm A / SKU rủi ro • Theo dõi KPI và duyệt thay đổi chính sách Conclusion: automate only after verifying data sources, access permissions, and approval workflows.
